claim: Mobile integrons are widespread genetic platforms that allow bacteria to modulate the expression of antibiotic resistance cassettes by shuffling their position from a common promoter.
source: Mobile integrons are widespread genetic platforms that allow bacteria to modulate the expression of antibiotic resistance cassettes by shuffling their position from a common promoter.
evidence: This is a general statement about integron function that is supported by established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Antibiotic stress induces the expression of an integrase that excises and integrates cassettes.
source: Antibiotic stress induces the expression of an integrase that excises and integrates cassettes
evidence: This statement is supported by citations in the manuscript (Guerin et al., 2009) and is part of established knowledge about integron function.

claim: Integrase activity accelerated evolution by increasing the expression of a gentamicin resistance cassette through duplications and by eliminating redundant cassettes.
source: Crucially, integrase activity accelerated evolution by increasing the expression of a gentamicin resistance cassette through duplications and by eliminating redundant cassettes.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental evolution study presented in the manuscript, supported by genomic sequencing data and survival analysis.

claim: There was no evidence of deleterious off-target effects of integrase activity.
source: Importantly, we found no evidence of deleterious off-target effects of integrase activity.
evidence: This conclusion is based on genomic sequencing data showing minimal chromosomal rearrangements in populations with active integrase.

claim: Integrons accelerate resistance evolution by rapidly generating combinatorial variation in cassette composition while maintaining genomic integrity.
source: In summary, integrons accelerate resistance evolution by rapidly generating combinatorial variation in cassette composition while maintaining genomic integrity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data showing cassette rearrangements without widespread chromosomal mutations.

claim: Mobile integrons have played an important role in the evolution of resistance in pathogenic bacteria.
source: These elements are typically associated with transposons and conjugative plasmids and have played an important role in the evolution of resistance in pathogenic bacteria (Partridge et al., 2018).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Partridge et al., 2018.

claim: Five classes of mobile integrons, based on the sequence of their integrase, have arisen independently through association with diverse mobile elements.
source: Five classes of MIs, based on the sequence of their integrase, have arisen independently through association with diverse mobile elements, but the class 1 integron is, by far, the most prevalent and clinically relevant.
evidence: This is established knowledge about integron classification.

claim: The class 1 integron is the most prevalent and clinically relevant mobile integron.
source: Five classes of MIs, based on the sequence of their integrase, have arisen independently through association with diverse mobile elements, but the class 1 integron is, by far, the most prevalent and clinically relevant.
evidence: This statement is supported by established knowledge and multiple citations in the manuscript.

claim: The first multidrug resistance plasmids isolated in the 1950s carried class 1 mobile integrons.
source: The first multidrug resistance plasmids that were isolated in the 1950s carried class 1 MIs (Liebert et al., 1999; Mitsuhashi et al., 1961; Rownd et al., 1966; Stokes and Hall, 1989)
evidence: This historical statement is supported by multiple citations.

claim: Class 1 integrons are found in a substantial fraction of isolates of Escherichia coli.
source: recent surveys have shown that class 1 integrons are found in a substantial fraction of isolates of Escherichia coli (Halaji et al., 2020; Rao et al., 2006; Yu et al., 2003)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to multiple survey studies.

claim: Class 1 integrons are found in a substantial fraction of isolates of Klebsiella pneumoniae.
source: recent surveys have shown that class 1 integrons are found in a substantial fraction of isolates of Escherichia coli (Halaji et al., 2020; Rao et al., 2006; Yu et al., 2003), Klebsiella pneumoniae (Firoozeh et al., 2019; Li et al., 2013)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to survey studies.

claim: Class 1 integrons are found in a substantial fraction of isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
source: recent surveys have shown that class 1 integrons are found in a substantial fraction of isolates of Escherichia coli (Halaji et al., 2020; Rao et al., 2006; Yu et al., 2003), Klebsiella pneumoniae (Firoozeh et al., 2019; Li et al., 2013), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (Oliver et al., 2015; Ruiz-Martínez et al., 2011)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to survey studies.

claim: Class 1 integrons are found in a substantial fraction of isolates of Acinetobacter baumanii.
source: recent surveys have shown that class 1 integrons are found in a substantial fraction of isolates of Escherichia coli (Halaji et al., 2020; Rao et al., 2006; Yu et al., 2003), Klebsiella pneumoniae (Firoozeh et al., 2019; Li et al., 2013), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (Oliver et al., 2015; Ruiz-Martínez et al., 2011), and Acinetobacter baumanii (Chen et al., 2015; Turton et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to survey studies.

claim: Mobile integrons consist of an integrase encoding gene named intI followed by a recombination site, attI.
source: Mobile integrons consist of an integrase encoding gene named intI followed by a recombination site, attI (Hall et al., 1991; Partridge et al., 2000)
evidence: This structural description is supported by citations.

claim: Mobile integrons contain a variable array of mobile gene cassettes, typically 2-5 in mobile integrons.
source: a variable array of mobile gene cassettes (typically 2–5 in mobile integrons) ending each in a characteristic hairpin recombination site called the attC site (Hall et al., 1991).
evidence: This structural description is supported by a citation and established knowledge.

claim: Integron cassettes usually lack a promoter, and their expression is driven by the Pc promoter located upstream of the array.
source: Integron cassettes usually lack a promoter, and their expression is driven by the Pc promoter located upstream of the array (Collis and Hall, 1995)
evidence: This statement about cassette expression is supported by a citation.

claim: Expression levels of integron cassettes are highest for cassettes closest to the promoter.
source: such that expression levels are highest for cassettes closest to the promoter (Collis and Hall, 1995).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation and is also demonstrated in the manuscript's own data (Figure 1c).

claim: The SOS response induces the expression of integrases.
source: The SOS response (named after the Morse code ...---...) induces the expression of integrases (Guerin et al., 2009)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Integron recombination is semi-conservative, as only the bottom strand of the cassette is excised from the array following a recombination pathway that includes a replication step.
source: A peculiarity of this system is that integron recombination is semi-conservative, as only the bottom strand of the cassette is excised from the array following a recombination pathway that includes a replication step (Loot et al., 2012).
evidence: This mechanistic description is supported by a citation.

claim: Cassette excision and re-integration can lead to either a 'cut and paste' outcome or a 'copy and paste' outcome.
source: The implication of this is that cassette excision and re-integration can lead to two different results: either a 'cut and paste' outcome, resulting in the movement of a cassette within an array, or a 'copy and paste' outcome, leading to the insertion of a duplicate copy of a cassette in the conserved array (Escudero et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement about recombination outcomes is supported by a citation and logical inference from the semi-conservative mechanism.

claim: Resistance levels to gentamicin declined as the aadB cassette moved further away from the integrase.
source: As expected, resistance levels to gentamicin declined as the aadB cassette moved further away from the integrase (Figure 1c).
evidence: This is a direct observation from experimental data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: There was a 6- to 24-fold difference in minimum inhibitory concentration between arrays containing aadB in first and second positions.
source: we observed a 6- to 24-fold difference in minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) between arrays containing aadB in first and second positions
evidence: This is a quantitative result from MIC measurements.

claim: There was a less than twofold difference in MIC between arrays with aadB in second and third places.
source: but a less than twofold difference between arrays with aadB in second and third places.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from MIC measurements.

claim: A steady decrease in aadB cassette transcription levels was observed depending on the cassette position.
source: Instead of a sharp drop, we observed a steady decrease depending on the cassette position (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: This is a direct observation from qPCR data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Two short open-reading frames contained within the attI site can substantially enhance the translation of a cassette lacking a Shine-Dalgarno sequence when the cassette is located in first position.
source: Previous work has shown that two short open-reading frames contained within the attI site can substantially enhance the translation of a cassette lacking a Shine–Dalgarno (SD) sequence when the cassette is located in first position (Hanau-Berçot et al., 2002; Papagiannitsis et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work.

claim: Cassette position can modulate translation levels.
source: showing that cassette position can also modulate translation levels (Hanau-Berçot et al., 2002; Jacquier et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: The aadB cassette contains a reduced Shine-Dalgarno box.
source: Interestingly, the aadB cassette contains a reduced SD box (Figure 1—figure supplement 1b)
evidence: This is an observation from sequence analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The steep gradient in gentamicin resistance between first and second positions was mostly due to decreased translation.
source: suggesting that the steep gradient in gentamicin resistance between first and second positions was mostly due to decreased translation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of the reduced SD box and the known role of attI ORFs in translation enhancement.

claim: No difference in initial gentamicin resistance was detected between strains with array A3 or the ΔintI1A3 mutant in the conditions of the evolution experiment.
source: Importantly, we did not detect any difference in initial gentamicin resistance (MICexp = 24 mg/L) between strains with array A3 or the ΔintI1A3 mutant in the conditions of the evolution experiment
evidence: This is a direct observation from MIC measurements.

claim: Populations of WTA3 with a functional integrase had a higher survival rate than those of the ΔintI1A3 mutant.
source: Crucially, populations of WTA3 populations with a functional integrase had a higher survival rate than those of the ΔintI1A3 mutant, showing that the integrase can increase evolvability for antibiotic resistance (Figure 2b; log-rank test: Chisq = 17.7, df = 1, p=3e-05).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental evolution study, supported by survival analysis and shown in Figure 2b.

claim: No extinctions were detected in either of the control treatments.
source: We did not detect any extinctions in either of the controls
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental evolution study.

claim: The higher extinction rate of ΔintI1A3 populations was driven by exposure to high doses of gentamicin.
source: showing that the higher extinction rate of ΔintI1A3 populations was driven by exposure to high doses of gentamicin.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison between ramping and control populations.

claim: A similar level of resistance was observed between ΔintI1A3 and WTA3 populations at the final time point.
source: We observed a similar level of resistance between ΔintI1A3 (mean MIC = 24,200 mg/L; s.d. = 1864; n = 5) and WTA3 (mean MIC = 27,800 mg/L; s.d. = 6031; n = 15) populations (t = 2.044, p=0.056)
evidence: This is a quantitative result from MIC measurements with statistical analysis.

claim: Integrase activity increased the likelihood of resistance evolution, but did not impact the final resistance levels of surviving populations.
source: showing that integrase activity increased the likelihood of resistance evolution, but did not impact the final resistance levels of surviving populations.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the survival and MIC data.

claim: Four novel integron structures were formed by insertion of the aadB cassette and/or deletions of blaVEB-1-dfrA5.
source: We found evidence for widespread cassette re-arrangement in WTA3 populations and identified four novel integron structures that were formed by insertion of the aadB cassette and/or deletions of blaVEB-1-dfrA5 (Figure 3a,b and Supplementary files 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The junction sites for cassette insertions and deletions were consistent with integrase activity.
source: The junction sites for cassette insertions and deletions were consistent with integrase activity: recombination happened at the 5′-GTT-3′ triplet of the attI1, attCaadB, and attCdfrA5 sites.
evidence: This is an observation from sequence analysis of rearrangement junctions.

claim: No evidence for cassette re-arrangements was found in ΔintI1A3 populations.
source: We did not find any evidence for cassette re-arrangements in ΔintI1A3 populations
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: No cassette re-arrangements were found in control WTA3 populations selected at a low dose of gentamicin.
source: or in control WTA3 populations that we selected at a low dose of gentamicin (×1/8 MIC)
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: The entire R388 plasmid was lost in all ΔintI1A3 and WTA3 populations passaged without antibiotic.
source: while the entire R388 plasmid was lost in all ΔintI1A3 and WTA3 populations passaged without antibiotic.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the control populations.

claim: Cassette re-arrangements were found in most populations at the ×4 MIC time point.
source: Cassette re-arrangements were found in most populations at the ×4 MIC time point
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Approximately 90% of populations contained cassette re-arrangements by the end of the experiment.
source: and approximately 90% of populations (19/21) contained cassette re-arrangements by the end of the experiment
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Integron structural polymorphisms were found in 50% of populations at ×4 MIC.
source: Integron structural polymorphisms were found in 50% of populations (12/24) at ×4 MIC
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Within-population diversity in integron structure was transient and almost all populations contained a single dominant integron structure by the final time point.
source: but this within-population diversity was transient and almost all populations contained a single dominant integron structure by the final time point.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing genomic sequencing data across time points.

claim: The most common novel integron structure contained a 'copy and paste' insertion of aadB in first position via attI × attCaadB recombination.
source: The most common novel integron structure contained a 'copy and paste' insertion of aadB in first position via attI × attCaadB recombination (ie aadB-blaVEB-1-dfrA5aadB).
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: The novel aadB-blaVEB-1-dfrA5-aadB integron is associated with a large increase (64-fold) in gentamicin resistance.
source: This novel integron is associated with a large increase (64-fold) in gentamicin resistance due to the dominant effect of first position on aadB, with similar levels to our constructed arrays with aadB in first position (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from MIC measurements shown in Figure 3e.

claim: No aadB-blaVEB-1-dfrA5 arrays were identified.
source: Interestingly, we did not identify any aadBblaVEB-1dfrA5 arrays, which would be the result of an aadB excision followed by reintegration of aadB in first position within the same array
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: The absence of aadB-blaVEB-1-dfrA5 arrays highlights the prevalence of 'copy and paste' cassette insertions.
source: highlighting the prevalence of 'copy and paste' cassette insertions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that only 'copy and paste' products were found.

claim: Degenerate integrons lacking the blaVEB-1 and dfrA5 cassettes were present at relatively high frequency at both the ×4 and ×1024 MIC time points.
source: Degenerate integrons that lack the blaVEB-1 and dfrA5 cassettes (i.e. either aadB or aadBaadB arrays) were also present at relatively high frequency at both the ×4 and ×1024 MIC time points.
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Degenerate arrays were always observed in conjunction with the aadB-blaVEB-1-dfrA5-aadB array and never with the ancestral array in mixed populations.
source: Interestingly, in mixed arrays populations, these reduced arrays were always observed in conjunction with the aadB-blaVEB-1dfrA5aadB array and never with the ancestral array.
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Degenerate arrays evolved via aadB insertion in first position, followed by en bloc deletion of the other cassettes.
source: This repeated association provides good evidence that degenerate arrays evolved via aadB insertion in first position, to form the common aadB-blaVEB-1dfrA5aadB array, followed by the en bloc deletion of the other cassettes (blaVEB-1dfrA5aadB or blaVEB-1dfrA5) to form aadB and aadBaadB arrays.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed association patterns in the data.

claim: Recombination for cassette deletions happened at the 5′-GTT-3′ triplet of the R box of attCaadB and attCdfrA5 sites.
source: Recombination happened at the 5′-GTT-3′ triplet of the R box of attCaadB and attCdfrA5 sites, suggesting that these deletions were driven by integrase activity
evidence: This is an observation from sequence analysis of deletion junctions.

claim: The second aadB cassette in the aadB-aadB array is redundant.
source: The relative prevalence of these two degenerate arrays did not change between the ×4 and ×1024 MIC time points (four aadB against three aadBaadB arrays at ×4 MIC and three aadB against three aadBaadB arrays at ×1024 MIC), which suggests that the second aadB cassette in the aadBaadB array is redundant.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of change in relative prevalence over time.

claim: There was a marginal difference (×2) in MIC between evolved plasmids carrying aadB and aadB-aadB.
source: In line with this argument, we found a marginal difference (×2) in MIC between evolved plasmids carrying aadB (mean = 512, s.d. = 0) and aadBaadB (mean = 939, s.d. = 121).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from MIC measurements.

claim: Arrays containing a duplicate copy of aadB at the end of the array (blaVEB-1-dfrA5-aadB-aadB) were only found at the ×4 MIC time point.
source: Finally, we found arrays containing a duplicate copy of aadB at the end of the array (blaVEB-1dfrA5aadBaadB), which are likely to have been formed by the insertion of an aadB cassette in the middle or at the end of the array through the less frequent attC × attC integration (intermolecular) reaction. These arrays were only found at the ×4 MIC time point
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: blaVEB-1-dfrA5-aadB-aadB arrays conferred a small increase in gentamicin resistance that was ultimately an evolutionary dead end under strong selection.
source: strongly suggesting that they conferred a small increase in gentamicin resistance that was ultimately an evolutionary dead end under strong selection for elevated resistance.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that these arrays were only found at the early time point.

claim: Mutations in blaVEB-1 were found in more than 80% of WTA3 and ΔintI1A3 populations from the ×4 MIC time point.
source: Mutations in blaVEB-1 were found in more than 80% of WTA3 and ΔintI1A3 populations from the ×4 MIC time point
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Mutations in blaVEB-1 were found in almost all populations where the blaVEB-1 cassette was maintained at the ×1024 MIC time point.
source: and in almost all populations where the blaVEB-1 cassette was maintained at the ×1024 MIC time point, including 5/6 ΔintI1A3 and 16/16 WTA3 populations.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: All mutations in blaVEB-1 were amino acid substitutions or indels.
source: All mutations in blaVEB-1 were amino acid substitutions (n = 9) or indels (n = 16)
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: The 23 amino acid signal peptide of blaVEB-1 was a hotspot for mutations.
source: and the 23 amino acid signal peptide was a hotspot for mutations (12 of 25 blaVEB-1 mutations)
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: There was strong selection to eliminate the secretion of the redundant blaVEB-1 resistance protein.
source: suggesting strong selection to eliminate the secretion of this redundant resistance protein
evidence: This is an inference based on the concentration of mutations in the signal peptide.

claim: Similar blaVEB-1 mutations were found in the ⅛ MIC controls.
source: Furthermore, similar blaVEB-1 mutations were also found in the ⅛ MIC controls
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: blaVEB-1 mutations were beneficial under low doses of gentamicin.
source: demonstrating that these mutations were beneficial under low doses of gentamicin, as we would expect if this cassette imposed an important fitness cost.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of similar mutations in control populations.

claim: Parallel evolution occurred close to the putative translation initiation site of the aadB cassette.
source: Parallel evolution also occurred close to the putative translation initiation site of the aadB cassette.
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Mutations near the aadB translation initiation site were very rare at the ×4 MIC time points but were present at a high frequency in ΔintI1A3 populations from the final time point.
source: These mutations were very rare at the ×4 MIC time points (2/46 populations), but were present at a high frequency in ΔintI1A3 populations from the final time point (4/6 populations)
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Mutations near the aadB translation initiation site are linked with high level of gentamicin resistance.
source: and are linked with high level of gentamicin resistance (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is an observation from MIC measurements shown in Figure 3e.

claim: Mutations near the aadB translation initiation site were favored in ΔintI1A3 populations as they increased the translation rate of the weakly expressed third position aadB cassette.
source: We speculate that these mutations were favored in ΔintI1A3 populations as they increased the translation rate of the weakly expressed third position aadB cassette and offer an alternative mechanism to increase aadB expression in the absence of re-arrangements.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed pattern of mutations.

claim: Chromosomal evolution occurred more rapidly in the ΔintI1A3 populations than in the WTA3 populations at ×4 MIC.
source: Chromosomal evolution occurred more rapidly in the ΔintI1A3 populations than in the WTA3 populations, as demonstrated by the high cumulative frequency of mutations in ΔintI1A3 populations (mean = 1.01; s.e. = 0.17, see Figure 4—figure supplement 2) at ×4 MIC compared to WTA3 populations (mean = 0.48; s.e. = 0.11; t = −2.69, df = 35.83, p=0.01, Welch two-sample t-test).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from genomic sequencing data with statistical analysis.

claim: Accelerated chromosomal evolution in the absence of integrase activity was short-lived.
source: However, accelerated chromosomal evolution in the absence of integrase activity was short-lived, and cumulative frequency of mutations in the WTA3 and ΔintI1A3 populations was almost identical at the end of the experiment (mean WTA3 = 2.45 SNPs; mean ΔintI1A3 = 2.65 SNPs, see Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Only one case of chromosomal recombination was found, with a 3.5 kb deletion between the two highly homologous ccoN1 and ccoN2 cytochrome C subunits in one WTA3 population.
source: Crucially, we found only one case of chromosomal recombination, with a 3.5 kb deletion between the two highly homologous ccoN1 and ccoN2 cytochrome C subunits in one WTA3 population (Supplementary file 2)
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Off-target effects of the integrase were undetectable in the experiment.
source: showing that off-target effects of the integrase were undetectable in our experiment, in spite of our extensive genomic sequencing.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the lack of observed chromosomal rearrangements.

claim: 41 different SNPs and 58 short indels were identified in eight intergenic regions and 41 genes.
source: In total, we identified 41 different SNPs and 58 short indels in eight intergenic regions and 41 genes, with a similar spectrum of mutations in the ramping WTA3 and ΔintI1A3 populations (Figure 4; Supplementary files 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a quantitative summary of genomic sequencing data.

claim: Many of the mutated genes have known roles in antibiotic resistance.
source: First, many of the mutated genes have known roles in antibiotic resistance; for example, 11/41 mutated genes have also been identified in an aminoglycoside resistance screen in P. aeruginosa (Schurek et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a previous screen.

claim: Parallel evolution was very common, occurring in 11 of 42 genes and 3 of 8 intergenic regions.
source: Second, parallel evolution was very common. Repeated evolution occurred in 11 of 42 (26%) genes and 3 of 8 (38%) intergenic regions with 68% of mutations occurring in these genes.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Only 1 of 41 mutations in coding regions was synonymous.
source: Only 1 of 41 mutations in coding regions was synonymous, providing evidence that the rapid evolution of proteins was driven by positive selection, and not simply by an elevated mutation rate.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: The rapid evolution of proteins was driven by positive selection, not by an elevated mutation rate.
source: providing evidence that the rapid evolution of proteins was driven by positive selection, and not simply by an elevated mutation rate.
evidence: This is an inference based on the low proportion of synonymous mutations.

claim: There was almost no overlap between the genes that were mutated in the ramping populations and the controls.
source: Finally, we found almost no overlap between the genes that were mutated in the ramping populations and the controls
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: The evolutionary response of the ramping populations was dominated by selection for high levels of gentamicin resistance.
source: implying that the evolutionary response of the ramping populations was dominated by selection for high levels of gentamicin resistance.
evidence: This is an inference based on the lack of overlap with control populations.

claim: For both control regimens, the chromosomal genes with the most mutations were cdrA and PA1874.
source: For both control regimens, the chromosomal genes with the most mutations were cdrA (PA4625), involved in biofilm formation (Reichhardt et al., 2018), and PA1874, a hypothetical protein.
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: No wide-scale chromosomal re-arrangements were observed in control populations.
source: Similarly to the ramping populations, no wide-scale chromosomal re-arrangements were observed
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: No major differences could be found between the distribution of mutations between WTA3 and ΔintI1A3 populations in both control regimens at x1024 MIC.
source: and no major differences could be found between the distribution of mutations between WTA3 and ΔintI1A3 populations in both control regimens at x1024 MIC (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The initial stages of adaptation to gentamicin were driven by mutations in a very diverse set of genes, with a strong bias toward genes involved in translation.
source: In the ramping populations, the initial stages of adaptation to gentamicin were driven by mutations in a very diverse set of genes, with a strong bias toward genes that are involved in translation, such as rluD and PA0668.4, which encodes for the 23S ribosomal RNA (Figure 4).
evidence: This is an observation from genomic sequencing data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Divergent mutational trajectories of evolution were observed in the WTA3 and ΔintI1A3 backgrounds.
source: Interestingly, we observed divergent mutational trajectories of evolution in the WTA3 and ΔintI1A3 backgrounds: the number of genes that were mutated in both backgrounds was small (n = 7) relative to the total number of mutated genes in either background (n = 26) and the correlation in mutation frequencies across backgrounds was weak (rho = 0.029; p=0.89 Spearman test).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from genomic sequencing data with statistical analysis.

claim: Chromosomal evolution became dominated by mutations in a few key target genes under continued selection for elevated gentamicin resistance.
source: Continued selection for elevated gentamicin resistance resulted in two changes in chromosomal evolution (Figure 4). First, chromosomal evolution became dominated by mutations in a few key target genes
evidence: This is an observation from genomic sequencing data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Many of the trajectories of chromosomal evolution followed during early adaptation ultimately led to evolutionary dead ends.
source: implying that many of the trajectories of chromosomal evolution followed during early adaptation ultimately led to evolutionary dead ends.
evidence: This is an inference based on the change in mutational targets over time.

claim: The correlation in mutation frequencies between early and late time points was very weak in both WTA3 and ΔintI1A3.
source: For example, the correlation in mutation frequencies between early and late time points was very weak, in both WTA3 (rho = −0.10, p=0.58) and ΔintI1A3 (rho = 0.20, p=0.307).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from statistical analysis of genomic sequencing data.

claim: Extensive parallel evolution was found in mexZ, amgS, and rluD in both the WTA3 and ΔintI1A3 populations.
source: In particular, we found evidence of extensive parallel evolution in mexZ, amgS, and rluD in both the WTA3 and ΔintI1A3 populations.
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: At a functional level, the mutations found at ×1024 MIC are predominantly involved in antibiotic efflux, as opposed to translation.
source: At a functional level, the mutations found at ×1024 MIC are predominantly involved in antibiotic efflux, as opposed to translation.
evidence: This is an observation from functional annotation of mutated genes.

claim: mexZ is a transcription factor that represses the expression of the mexXY multidrug efflux pump operon.
source: mexZ is a transcription factor that represses the expression of the mexXY multidrug efflux pump operon.
evidence: This is established knowledge about mexZ function.

claim: Mutations inactivating mexZ cause a 2- to 16-fold increase in aminoglycoside resistance.
source: Mutations inactivating mexZ cause a 2- to 16-fold increase in aminoglycoside resistance and have been widely identified in aminoglycoside-resistant P. aeruginosa isolates found in cystic fibrosis patients (Vogne et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: AmgS is part of an envelope stress-responsive two-component system AmgRS.
source: AmgS is part of an envelope stress-responsive two-component system AmgRS (Lau et al., 2013)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: amgS mutations upregulate the mexXY multidrug efflux system in the presence of aminoglycosides.
source: and amgS mutations upregulate the mexXY multidrug efflux system in the presence of aminoglycosides (Lau et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Mobile integrons carrying multiple blaVIM-1 carbapenemase cassettes have been found in clinical isolates of P. aeruginosa.
source: Interestingly, mobile integrons carrying multiple blaVIM-1 carbapenemase cassettes have been found in clinical isolates of P. aeruginosa (San Millan et al., 2015b)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Cassette duplications may play an important role in clinical settings.
source: suggesting that cassette duplications may play an important role in clinical settings.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observation of duplications in clinical isolates.

claim: PCR screening of populations that survived at ×2 MIC identified numerous cassette re-arrangements of both the blaVIM-1 and aadB cassettes.
source: PCR screening of populations that survived at ×2 MIC identified numerous cassette re-arrangements of both the blaVIM-1 and aadB cassettes, with potential blaVIM-1 duplications occurring in all 14 surviving populations (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a direct observation from PCR screening shown in Figure 5.

claim: Potential blaVIM-1 duplications occurred in all 14 surviving pAMBL1 populations at ×2 MIC.
source: with potential blaVIM-1 duplications occurring in all 14 surviving populations (Figure 5).
evidence: This is a direct observation from PCR screening shown in Figure 5.

claim: Short-read sequencing of clones isolated from two pAMBL1 populations confirmed the presence of duplications, with increased copy number of blaVIM-1 per plasmid.
source: Short-read sequencing of clones isolated from two of these populations confirmed the presence of duplications, as demonstrated by increased copy number of blaVIM-1 per plasmid (2.0 copies/plasmid [95% CI: 1.90–2.10] and 2.67 copies/plasmid [95% CI: 2.53–2.78]).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from sequencing data.

claim: 'Copy and paste' outcomes of cassette re-arrangements can drive the rapid evolution of elevated carbapenem resistance.
source: Although it is not possible to definitely prove the role of the integrase without control populations lacking a functional integrase, these results strongly support the idea that 'copy and paste' outcomes of cassette re-arrangements can drive the rapid evolution of elevated carbapenem resistance
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of blaVIM-1 duplications under meropenem selection.

claim: 'Copy and paste' cassette rearrangement was the mechanism behind the blaVIM-1 amplification observed in the plasmid pAMBL2 isolated in the same hospital.
source: and was the mechanism behind the blaVIM-1 amplification observed in the plasmid pAMBL2 isolated in the same hospital (San Millan et al., 2015b).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results and a citation to a previous study.

claim: Integrase activity accelerated the evolution of gentamicin resistance through rapid and repeated re-shuffling of the aadB resistance cassette.
source: Crucially, integrase activity accelerated the evolution of gentamicin resistance through rapid and repeated re-shuffling of the aadB resistance cassette, providing experimental support for the 'adaptation on demand' hypothesis.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion from the experimental evolution study.

claim: All of the aadB re-arrangements observed were 'copy and paste' outcomes, resulting in the duplication of aadB.
source: Strikingly, all of the aadB re-arrangements that we observed were 'copy and paste' outcomes, resulting in the duplication of aadB (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data shown in Figure 6.

claim: A bias towards evolution by 'copy and paste' is expected if increased copy number of the cassette under selection is beneficial.
source: A bias towards evolution by 'copy and paste' is expected if increased copy number of the cassette under selection is beneficial.
evidence: This is a logical inference about evolutionary dynamics.

claim: The integrase enzyme may be inherently biased towards 'copy and paste' cassette re-arrangement, potentially by favoring the reinsertion of an excised cassette into the conserved array.
source: However, the absence of any 'cut and paste' products in our experiments, instead of the expected 30%, suggests that the integrase enzyme may be inherently biased towards 'copy and paste' cassette re-arrangement, potentially by favoring the reinsertion of an excised cassette into the conserved array.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed bias in recombination outcomes.

claim: Duplicate cassettes are only found in 5% of the integrons that contain two or more cassettes in the INTEGRALL database.
source: For example, duplicate cassettes are only found in 5% of the integrons that contain two or more cassettes in the INTEGRALL database (Moura et al., 2009; Supplementary file 4).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from database analysis.

claim: Difficulties associated with resolving duplications from short-read sequencing data probably contribute to the rarity of duplicate cassettes in databases.
source: Difficulties associated with resolving duplications from short-read sequencing data probably contribute to this (Alkan et al., 2011)
evidence: This is a speculation supported by a citation about sequencing limitations.

claim: The duplicate copies of selected cassettes created by 'copy and paste' re-shuffling facilitate the loss of redundant cassettes.
source: Interestingly, the duplicate copies of selected cassettes created by 'copy and paste' re-shuffling facilitate the loss of redundant cassettes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed patterns of cassette loss following duplication.

claim: Duplication of cassettes with highly recombinogenic attC sites facilitates the integrase-mediated excision of redundant cassettes.
source: First, duplication of cassettes with highly recombinogenic attC sites, such as aadB, facilitates the integrase-mediated excision of redundant cassettes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed patterns of cassette loss.

claim: Homologous recombination between duplicate cassettes or between copies of integrons on different plasmids provides a second mechanism for integron degeneration.
source: Homologous recombination between duplicate cassettes or between copies of integrons on different plasmids provides a second mechanism for integron degeneration (Andersson and Hughes, 2009)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Extremely mobile cassettes, such as aadB, can compensate for the lack of mobility of other less recombinogenic cassettes, like blaVEB-1.
source: This also highlights how extremely mobile cassettes, such as aadB, can compensate for the lack of mobility of other less recombinogenic cassettes, like blaVEB-1 (Aubert et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed patterns of cassette rearrangement, supported by a citation.

claim: The constitutive expression of cassettes from the Pc promoter ensures that redundant cassettes impose a fitness cost.
source: The constitutive expression of cassettes from the Pc promoter ensures that redundant cassettes impose a fitness cost (Lacotte et al., 2017)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Selection for cassette loss is likely to be common.
source: implying that selection for cassette loss is likely to be common.
evidence: This is an inference based on the fitness cost of redundant cassettes.

claim: The semi-conservative nature of cassette excision is key to the evolutionary benefits of integrase activity.
source: Given this, we argue that semi-conservative nature of cassette excision is key to the evolutionary benefits of integrase activity, as it allows integrons to rapidly gain additional copies of selected cassettes and facilitates the subsequent elimination of costly redundant cassettes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observed patterns of cassette duplication and loss.

claim: Mutations in the chromosome and in the integron made an important contribution to resistance evolution.
source: In our experiments, mutations in the chromosome and in the integron made an important contribution to resistance evolution and are key to understanding the effective integrase evolutionary benefits.
evidence: This is an observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Integrase activity was associated with the loss of the redundant blaVEB-1 cassette.
source: For example, integrase activity was associated with the loss of the redundant blaVEB-1 cassette, which is in line with the integrase-mediated loss of redundant cassettes during selection for elevated chloramphenicol resistance observed by Barraud and Ploy, 2015.
evidence: This is an observation from genomic sequencing data, supported by a citation to a similar finding.

claim: The blaVEB-1 cassette was rapidly inactivated by mutations in ΔintI1 populations.
source: However, the blaVEB-1 cassette was also rapidly inactivated by mutations in ΔintI1 populations.
evidence: This is a direct observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Mutations in the promoter of the aadB cassette provided an alternative mechanism to increase the expression of this cassette that did not depend on integrase activity.
source: Similarly, mutations in the promoter of the aadB cassette provided an alternative mechanism to increase the expression of this cassette that did not depend on integrase activity.
evidence: This is an observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: P. aeruginosa has a strong potential to adapt to aminoglycosides via chromosomal mutations.
source: Moreover, P. aeruginosa has a strong potential to adapt to aminoglycosides via chromosomal mutations (López-Causapé et al., 2018; Schurek et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: An even stronger impact of the integrase should be observable in environments or species where evolution possibilities through mutations are more limited.
source: Given our populations possess a sizable evolvability potential through mutations, even in the absence of integrase activity, we hypothesize an even stronger impact of the integrase should be observable in environments or species where evolution possibilities through mutations are more limited.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the observed results.

claim: There was a divergence in the evolution of the two genotypes at the early ×4 MIC time point.
source: Finally, we detected an interesting interplay between chromosomal evolution and integrase activity, with a divergence in the evolution of the two genotypes at the early ×4 MIC time point, which is potentially the most clinically relevant.
evidence: This is an observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Rapid chromosomal and plasmid evolution via mutations across a wide range of target genes allowed populations lacking a functional integrase to evolve resistance to increasing concentrations of gentamicin.
source: Rapid chromosomal and plasmid evolution via mutations across a wide range of target genes allowed populations lacking a functional integrase to evolve resistance to increasing concentrations of gentamicin.
evidence: This is an observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Wild-type populations showed a much-reduced mutation prevalence, as chromosomal mutations were potentially out-competed by the frequent and more efficient cassette re-arrangements.
source: The wild-type populations, on the other hand, showed a much-reduced mutation prevalence, as chromosomal mutations were potentially out-competed by the frequent and more efficient cassette re-arrangements.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed difference in mutation prevalence.

claim: Accelerated chromosomal evolution in ΔintI1A3 populations was short lived.
source: This accelerated chromosomal evolution in ΔintI1A3 populations was short lived, confirming that rapid evolution was driven by more effective selection for mutations in populations lacking an integrase, rather than a difference in mutation rate per se.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the temporal dynamics of mutation accumulation.

claim: All populations that were able to survive very high levels of gentamicin exposure evolved by mutations of a common suite of target genes involved in antibiotic efflux and ribosomal modification.
source: All populations that were able to survive very high levels of gentamicin exposure evolved by mutations of a common suite of target genes involved in antibiotic efflux and ribosomal modification
evidence: This is an observation from genomic sequencing data.

claim: Integrase activity did not ultimately alter the mutational routes to high-level resistance, but can impact chromosomal evolution during the early evolution of resistance.
source: highlighting the fact that integrase activity did not ultimately alter the mutational routes to high-level resistance, but can impact chromosomal evolution during the early evolution of resistance.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of mutational patterns across genotypes and time points.

claim: Systems that upregulate the mutation rate under stress are widespread in bacteria.
source: Systems that upregulate the mutation rate under stress are widespread in bacteria (Foster, 2011; MacLean et al., 2013)
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: Beneficial mutations generated by stress-induced mutagenesis systems can accelerate adaptation to stress.
source: and beneficial mutations generated by these systems can accelerate adaptation to stress (but see Torres-Barceló et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: Most of the mutations generated by stress-induced mutagenesis systems will be deleterious.
source: However, most of the mutations generated by these systems will be deleterious
evidence: This is established knowledge about mutation effects.

claim: Stress-induced mutagenesis will tend to reduce fitness, particularly if the deleterious effects of mutations are exacerbated by stress.
source: and stress-induced mutagenesis will therefore tend to reduce fitness, particularly if the deleterious effects of mutations are exacerbated by stress (Kishony and Leibler, 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: The integron integrase is known to have off-target activity.
source: The integron integrase is known to have off-target activity (Recchia et al., 1994)
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation.

claim: The costs associated with off-target recombination contribute to the cost of integrase expression.
source: and it has been argued that the costs associated with off-target recombination contribute to the cost of integrase expression (Harms et al., 2013), limiting the evolutionary benefit of this system (Engelstädter et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations.

claim: No evidence of chromosomal re-arrangements or increased mutation rates could be linked to integrase activity, with the exception of a single deletion in the R388 plasmid.
source: We found no evidence of chromosomal re-arrangements or increased mutation rates that could be linked to integrase activity, with the exception of a single deletion in the R388 plasmid that was suggestive of integrase activity, suggesting a low rate of off-target recombination.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on genomic sequencing data.

claim: Integrase activity allows bacteria to modulate cassette expression, rapidly gain additional copies of selected cassettes and eliminate redundant cassettes, while the high specificity of integrase-mediated recombination maintains genomic integrity.
source: Integrase activity allows bacteria to modulate cassette expression, rapidly gain additional copies of selected cassettes and eliminate redundant cassettes, while the high specificity of integrase-mediated recombination maintains genomic integrity, minimizing the costs of integrase activity.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental data.

claim: Integrase activity will accelerate resistance evolution most for highly mobile cassettes that display strong positional effects, such as aadB.
source: Given the importance of cassette re-shuffling, we argue that integrase activity will accelerate resistance evolution most for highly mobile cassettes that display strong positional effects, such as aadB.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental results.

claim: Cassette re-shuffling will be most important in cases where bacteria have limited ability to adapt to antibiotics.
source: Given this, we argue that cassette re-shuffling will be most important in cases where bacteria have limited ability to adapt to antibiotics, for example when only a small number of mutations can increase resistance, or where resistance mutations carry large fitness costs.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the experimental results.

claim: Treatment strategies should seek to target integrons, for example by combining antibiotics with adjuvants that limit integrase activity by inhibiting the SOS response.
source: Our work also supports the view that treatment strategies should seek to target integrons, for example by combining antibiotics with adjuvants that limit integrase activity by inhibiting the SOS response (Hocquet et al., 2012), or by using combinations of antibiotics that impose conflicting selective pressures on the integron.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the study's findings, supported by a citation.
